newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia needs $5 bln to destroy chemical weapons.
newsitem.headline: Russia needs $5 bln to destroy chemical weapons.

text.p: Russia needs more than $5 billion to destroy its vast arsenal of chemical weapons, Interfax news agency quoted the head of the country's chemical and biological defence force as saying on Friday.

Colonel-General Stanislav Petrov said although the programme, which calls for the destruction of 40,000 tonnes of chemical weapons, lacked sufficient domestic financing, Russia could not rely heavily on foreign help.
"(Foreign countries) are not rushing to provide Russia with financial assistance in this area," the general said.

He said that in 1996 one percent of the required sum was earmarked for the programme from the budget, while foreign cash from Germany and the United States would not account for more than 3.5 percent of the cost.
Petrov said that given stable financing Russia could destroy its chemical weapons completely by 2007. Interfax quoted him as saying more than $5 billion was required overall.
Petrov's comments sounded like an indirect appeal for more help from the West. Russia has more than once said it has no money to eliminate its chemical stockpile.

Russia's parliament resisted international pressure in April to ratify a treaty banning chemical weapons, appealing for a significant increase in financial aid and a possible extension of the period for liquidating its chemical arsenals.
The United States and Germany have already given Russia millions of dollars to help with chemical weapons destruction.

Russian ministers promised on Friday to spend more money on defence next year, and to increase military expenditure further annually, but the money is needed for long-delayed military reform, which is intended to convert Russia's 1.8 million-strong conscript army into a compact professional force by 2000.
